doc_description: A synthetic Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement for North Basin Industrial Park, Nevada (effective 10 March 2027) between Westmere Industrial Park Authority and Sunhaven Energy Operations Ltd., covering the 7.5 MWdc solar, 4 MW/16 MWh battery and six-transformer asset scope, a 2027–2032 term, fee and performance terms, and liability, default, exit and Reno mediation provisions.

structure.title: Page 001 - Parties, Purpose and Contract Structure
structure.summary: A synthetic Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement for North Basin Industrial Park, Nevada, between Westmere Industrial Park Authority (Owner) and Sunhaven Energy Operations Ltd. (Operator), effective 10 March 2027. Covers parties and purpose: Operator performs preventive and corrective maintenance, remote monitoring and reporting, cannot act as electricity retailer, and must follow the Owner's dispatch protocol. Establishes order of precedence among the agreement and Appendices A (assets), B (safety plan), and C (reporting templates), with amendments controlling only as expressly stated. Defines the asset scope (7.5 MWdc solar PV, 4 MW/16 MWh LFP battery, six MV transformers, site SCADA) across two yards, exclusions (utility feeder, tenant circuits, third-party telecom), and a 30-day asset record reconciliation with a 2% discrepancy escalation threshold. Sets a five-year term from 1 May 2027 to 30 April 2032, with one optional two-year extension, plus mobilization within 20 Business Days and a joint handover report that does not waive pre-existing defects. Fees: USD 42,000 monthly fixed fee; parts over USD 2,500 need written approval except safety emergencies; USD 145/hour emergency labor; monthly invoicing in arrears, 25-day payment terms, and 0.75% monthly late interest.

structure.title: Page 002 - Asset Register and Operating Boundaries

Fees include USD 42,000 monthly fixed fee, parts over USD 2,500 requiring approval (emergency exceptions), USD 145/hour emergency labor, and monthly invoicing with 25-day payment and 0.75% monthly late interest.

structure.title: Page 005 - Preventive Maintenance and Response Times
structure.summary: Covers preventive maintenance (monthly inverter inspections, quarterly infrared thermography, annual protective relay testing, six-monthly battery fire-suppression checks, asset-tagged records) and incident response (Critical Incidents: remote acknowledgement in 10 minutes, on-site attendance in two hours; High Incidents affecting over 20% capacity: acknowledgement in 30 minutes). Deferral of maintenance is allowed only for weather, permit or safety reasons, with documented justification and Owner-approved revised dates. Performance guarantees include 98.5% annual PV availability, no guaranteed battery throughput since Owner controls dispatch, and a fee reduction of 1% per 0.5-point shortfall capped at 6%. Safety requires permits, lockout-tagout, arc-flash controls, an emergency plan and two drills yearly. Environmental rules cover regulated battery waste and one-hour electrolyte release reporting. Monthly reports are due by the fifth Business Day, with telemetry kept 24 months. Critical spares, subcontracting with prior approval, cybersecurity controls with two-hour breach notification, and insurance minimums (employer liability, USD 3M general liability, USD 2M professional liability) are also addressed.

structure.title: Page 006 - Performance Guarantees and Adjustments
structure.summary: Covers an operator's obligations for a microgrid/solar-plus-storage site: preventive maintenance schedules (monthly inverter inspections, quarterly thermography, annual relay tests, six-monthly fire-suppression checks) and recording against asset IDs; incident response times (Critical: 10-minute remote acknowledgement, two-hour on-site attendance; High: 30-minute acknowledgement); and conditions for deferring maintenance with owner approval. Performance guarantees include 98.5% annual PV availability, no guaranteed battery throughput, and a fee reduction of 1% per 0.5-point shortfall capped at 6%. Safety requirements cover permits, lockout-tagout, arc-flash controls, emergency plans and drills. Environmental duties include regulated battery waste handling and one-hour electrolyte release reporting. Reporting requires monthly performance reports by the fifth business day and 24-month telemetry retention. Also addressed are critical spare parts stock and replenishment, subcontracting approval and liability, cybersecurity controls with two-hour breach notice, and insurance minimums (employer liability, USD 3M general liability, USD 2M professional liability).

structure.title: Page 009 - Insurance, Liability and Termination
structure.summary: The text covers a microgrid operations and maintenance agreement across pages 5-10. It specifies a preventive maintenance plan (monthly inverter inspections, quarterly thermography, annual relay tests, six-monthly battery fire-suppression checks, asset-linked records) and incident response times (Critical Incidents: remote acknowledgement in 10 minutes, on-site attendance in two hours; High Incidents: acknowledgement in 30 minutes), plus deferral conditions. It sets a 98.5% PV availability guarantee, excluding grid outages, maintenance and force majeure, with a fee reduction capped at 6%, and states no guaranteed battery throughput. Safety requirements include permits, lockout-tagout, arc-flash controls, emergency plans and drills. Environmental duties cover regulated battery waste and one-hour electrolyte release reporting. Reporting requires monthly performance reports and 24-month telemetry retention. Spare parts minimums, subcontracting approval, and cybersecurity controls with two-hour breach notice are included. Insurance limits, a liability cap at 100% of twelve months' fees, and default/termination rules are set. Exit support, formal notice rules, Nevada law, and mediation in Reno are also addressed.

structure.title: Page 010 - Exit Assistance, Notices and Disputes
structure.summary: Covers contractual liability and default terms: Operator's aggregate liability is capped at 100% of fixed service fees paid or payable in the prior twelve months, excluding fraud, intentional wrongdoing, and negligent bodily injury. A material nonmonetary breach may be cured within 30 days of written notice, and termination is permitted after three repeated Critical Incident response failures within any rolling twelve months, following an opportunity to respond. Exit support covers the final 45 days of the term, requiring delivery of a defect register, asset inventory, inspection history, and operating credentials to the replacement operator; work beyond 40 labor-hours is billed at USD 95/hour with prior written approval. Formal notices must be sent by courier or registered mail to signature-page addresses, with optional email copies; helpdesk messages do not qualify. Nevada law governs, and parties must attempt good-faith mediation in Reno, Nevada, for at least 20 Business Days before filing an ordinary contractual lawsuit.
